notes: Hand labels for the 67 near-dup pairs (cos>=0.78) on the live corpus. same = the two records state ONE fact in two vintages (collapse is correct). diff = two distinct facts that merely share a topic (collapse is wrong). ambig = genuinely borderline, excluded from scoring. CORRECTED 2026-10-21: 1064/1065 and 1064/1066 are 'diff', not 'same'. #1064 states what the port CONTAINS (7 themes ported, typed manifests, svelte-check/build/tests); #1065/#1066 state the DEPLOYMENT state (pushed, vercel promote, merged to main). Two distinct facts sharing a topic. Calibrated against 948/949 (both describe the cutover arrangement -> same) and 907/916 (explicit supersession -> same). CORRECTED 2026-10-21 (2nd pass, criterion 'same = the two records assert the SAME thing in two vintages'): 1063/1065, 853/891 and 890/891 are 'diff'. 1064 states what the port CONTAINS, 1065/1066 the DEPLOYMENT; 1063 the deployment setup gotchas, 1065 the cutover completion; 853 a routing map over 4 model names, 891 the systemone API contract; 890 OpenChamber's classification-provider role, 891 the 9router endpoint. Kept as 'same' because the later explicitly obsoletes the earlier: 855 'Removed CF Workers AI code', 849 'Correction 2026-09-26', 810 'after the first spacing pass', 1096 'was PUSHED', 1063/1065 and 803/810 audited. CORRECTED 2026-10-21 (3rd pass): 803/810 is diff — #810 also records a separate Maps layout change, while #803 holds the 76px virtual estimate, the 473-item verification and deploy a1093a85 that #810 does not. Both models said diff; the label was wrong. CORRECTED 2026-10-21 (4th pass): 1096/1099 is 'same', not 'diff' - the model was right and the label was wrong. Both notes are the SAME 'Portal (me.mcky.space) status' note, one refreshed: #1099 restates every technical detail of #1096 (SignInForm useSignIn create/password/finalize, LINE signIn.sso with redirectCallbackUrl, App rendering <HandleSSOCallback> at ?sso_callback=1, the App split into wrapper + PortalApp) and advances the state from 'branch clerk-signal-api 29b9cf3 NOT pushed/merged' to 'MERGED to main (fast-forward 91dce00..29b9cf3) and PUSHED -> deployed'. Both carry the same 'real E2E login not run' caveat and are dated 2026-10-16. The discriminator used for the 3rd pass still holds in the other direction: 1063/1065 is 'diff' because #1065 does NOT restate #1063's content (it drops the project choice and every gotcha), whereas #1099 restates #1096 in full. Rule for the audit: B is a later vintage of A when B re-states A's substance and advances its state; a note that only shares a topic, or that replaces A's substance with a different assertion, is a different fact. CORRECTED 2026-10-21 (5th pass, the 8th wrong label): 1093/1099 is 'same', not 'diff'. The model was right and the label was wrong, and the relation graph settles it: #1096 supersedes #1093 and #1099 supersedes #1096, so #1093 is ALREADY declared a stale vintage of #1099 by the stored edges - a label of 'diff' made the data contradict itself. The judge agreed independently ('Later note updates the migration status from not pushed to pushed'). The tension: by the 'restates the substance IN FULL' test used for 1063/1065 it would be 'diff' (#1099 does not repeat #1093's package versions, and its primary subject is the Signal API commit 29b9cf3, not the Core 3 commit 91dce00). It is 'same' because the test already accepted for 1093/1096 - a status note that advances the same migration's state, without repeating the package details - is 'same', and consistency with that accepted label decides it. What makes it urgent rather than academic: the recall path returned #1093 ('NOT pushed') and #1099 ('MERGED and PUSHED') in the SAME result, because a chain only shadowed its root when the middle vintage happened to be in the results. Two different answers to the same question, depending on which notes the vector search happened to return. The fix is in the code (closeRelations + the relation is the authority, cosine no longer vetoes it), not in the label alone. FIFTH LABEL PASS 2026-10-21 — the eighth wrong label, and the reason it was wrong. #1093/#1099 was labelled 'diff' and is 'same'. The relation graph settles it: #1096 supersedes #1093 and #1099 supersedes #1096, so the stored edges already declared #1093 a stale vintage of #1099, and a label of 'diff' made the data contradict itself. The judge agreed independently (SAME, three votes, and the same verdict in the production run), and the merge test agrees: merging #1093 ('Clerk Core 3 migrated, NOT pushed') with #1099 ('Signal API MERGED and PUSHED, both live') gives one coherent statement, not two. The tension is honest and recorded here: #1099 does not repeat #1093's package versions, so by the 'restates the substance in full' test used for #1063/#1065 it would be 'diff'. It is 'same' because consistency with the already-accepted #1093/#1096 decides it — a status note that advances the same migration's state without repeating the package details is 'same' — and because the relation graph already says so. What makes it urgent rather than academic: the recall path returned #1093 ('NOT pushed') and #1099 ('MERGED and PUSHED') in the SAME result, because a chain only shadowed its root when the middle vintage happened to be in the results. Two answers to the same question, depending on which notes the vector search returned. The fix is in the code (closeRelations, and the relation is the authority in the collapse — cosine no longer vetoes it), not in the label alone. Also in this pass: #879/#884 firmed up from 'ambig' to 'same' (the live relation already asserted it and the merge test agrees — #884 is the branch-display round revised from the previous round, and the judge never ruled on it because it was borderline). The seven remaining judge/label disagreements are deliberate, and each has an independent reason rather than a vote: four where the label says 'same' and the judge is conservative — #591/#595 (the same 2026-08-27 vault rebuild recorded twice, once as a daily note and once as a session note), #1079/#1081 (a version bump, which the judge's own prompt calls 'the same fact'), #1078/#1083 (a later state that absorbs the earlier — #1083 states the scout model fix it supersedes), #881/#999 (the corrected service recipe: 'sup is a sudo wrapper, not a service manager' is a later vintage of the same claim) — and three where the label says 'diff': #879/#885 and #879/#886, which the judge calls SAME 9 times out of 9, where collapsing them transitively would delete the still-current list-page rule through the display chain (#884), so the feature must not collapse them; and #924/#935, an incident log against the service-management note that corrects it, where the judge itself splits (7 of 9 DIFF). Audit the ground truth in both directions: 8 wrong labels so far, 6 found by trusting the label over the judge and 2 by trusting the judge over the label. | SIXTH CORRECTION 2026-10-21: #591/#595 is 'diff', not 'same'. The daily note (#591) and the session note (#595) record the same 2026-08-27 vault rebuild, but they assert different things (#591: the rebuild plus what was still pending -- the creds path, the backup path, the Obsidian plugin list; #595: the rebuild plus the architecture decisions). A supersede relation says 'the older note is a stale vintage of the newer one'; #595 does not re-state #591's substance and does not advance it, so hiding #591 would lose facts the newer note does not carry. The adjudicator called it DIFF twice (the 3-vote judge and the curator run), and reading the two notes confirms the DIFF. This is the one label in the set that changed because the *operational* test disagreed with the merge test: a pair can be 'about the same event' and still be two facts.
